sasha: Heads up — we just saw a sharp p99 latency jump on chat_prod (~03:12 UTC). p50 unchanged, p95 up ~30ms, p99 spiked from 420ms -> 1.8s. Throughput dropped ~18%. Alert from infra-bot below.

infra-bot: [ALERT] route=chat_prod p99>1.5s for 3m, affected_hosts=pod-21, pod-34, pod-56

max: Any recent kernel/heuristic deploys?

kyung: Rolled a kernel selection tweak two hours ago that prefers the new fused-attn kernel for seq lengths <= 1024 but falls back to a compatibility kernel for mixed shapes. Logs show a batch with avg_seq_len=1387 forced fallback and then kernel choice oscillated. Posting profiler snippets.

kyung: ```
kernel_decision.log: 
[03:11:58] batch_id=9763 avg_seq=1387 model=mosaic-7b variant=fp16 -> selected_kernel=fallback_compat
[03:11:59] batch_id=9769 avg_seq=60 model=mosaic-7b variant=fp16 -> selected_kernel=fused_attn
[03:12:00] selected_kernel switched back and forth 4x in 2s -> latency amplification
```

alice: kvcache_stats for chat_prod route: 
```
route=chat_prod kv_hits=12.3% kv_misses=87.7% evictions=4.2k last_minute_evictions=1.9k
active_entries=138k avg_entry_size=1.2MB
```
Looks like eviction churn at the same time window.

sasha: Do we have a request-level pattern? Any ultra-long prompts or tool loops?

kyung: Sampling shows a cluster of requests with tool-calling loops. One session repeatedly called /tool:fetch_docs which appended long blobs each turn -> sequence lengths > 8k for those streams. Streaming backpressure meant some requests waited in the queue and got batched with short requests, causing large variance.

jonah: So the combo is: noisy tenant (tool loop) -> huge seq lengths -> KV cache thrash (evictions) -> kernel selection flip -> systemic latency spike. Classic cascade.

max: Can we mitigate quickly by isolation? Options: 1) route noisy tenant to a lower-priority pool, 2) throttle streaming tool calls, 3) tweak batching heuristic to not mix >1024 length items with short ones.

kyung: I ran a quick patch locally: if batch_stddev_seq_len > 800 then cap batch_size to 4 and prefer fused_attn by padding small ones rather than fallback. Locally p99 dropped back to ~380ms in replay. Patch diff: 
```
- if batch_size > CONFIG.MAX_BATCH: proceed
+ if batch_stddev_seq_len > 800: batch_size = min(batch_size, 4)
```

alice: Applied a short TTL increase for KV entries for chat_prod (temp) and lowered eviction aggressiveness on pod-56. That reduced evictions by ~60% in the last minute.

sasha: Any rollback options if heuristic patch causes regressions?

kyung: We can pin kernel selection to v1.11-legacy for chat_prod while we test. Command: 
```
redwoodctl route update chat_prod --kernel v1.11-legacy --reason "temp mitigate kernel oscillation"
```
I'll hold on executing until we agree.

jonah: I vote for two-step: 1) apply per-tenant emergency routing for the noisy tenant to dedicated pool (rate-limit tool calls), 2) apply the batching cap heuristic as a hotfix behind a feature flag.

max: +1. Also add a quick eval to detect tool-call loops by looking for repeated tool invocations > 5 in 30s and auto-throttle.

sasha: Ok go for emergency routing + feature-flagged batching cap. kyung, alice — coordinate and post exact commands here before executing. jonah, can you open a short PR for the loop detector?

kyung: Will post commands now. Planning to run kernel pin only if the batching cap doesn't stabilize p99 within 5m.

alice: Routing command I'm running: 
```
redwoodctl tenant route-override --tenant noisy-tenant --pool isolated-small --rate-limit 10r/s --duration 30m
```
Applying now.

kyung: Hotfix deployment (feature flag off by default): 
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/serve-runtime BATCH_STDDEV_CAP=800 BATCH_MAX_OVERRIDE=4
```
Rolling to pod-21 first.

infra-bot: [INFO] route-override applied for noisy-tenant -> isolated-small (duration 30m)

max: seeing immediate improvement on the affected pods: p99 down to ~430ms and throughput recovering. Keep monitoring for 10m.

sasha: Nice. Once stable, let's schedule a follow-up to: 1) harden kvcache TTL heuristics, 2) add kernel-selection hysteresis to avoid flip-flop, 3) implement loop detector + auto-throttle.

jonah: I'll open the PR for loop detector and add unit tests. ETA 2h.

sasha: Great. Thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:

kyung: Filing a postmortem draft with traces and profiler output in #postmortems after we collect full traces.

alice: I'll capture kvcache histograms and eviction chain for the postmortem.

max: And I'll add a backstop metric: batch_kernel_flip_rate to alert earlier.

sasha: Closing thread here. If anything regresses, re-open or ping. :thumbsup:
